criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-gate`. For each of the seven commit ids named in the request there is a test in which the commit is a pre-C0 hand change excused when its legacy-exempt entry is present. A second test fails with the same violation as today's check_history when the entry is absent. All pass.
criteria.evidence: `each_named_commit_is_excused_when_its_entry_is_present` loops over all seven names. For each one it builds a repo whose hand-change commit stands in for that name, writes a record naming it, and asserts no findings and no violations. `each_named_commit_fails_as_today_when_its_entry_is_absent` asserts the violations equal both `check_history` and `check_history_with_exempt(Some(vec![]))`, and include an Invariant violation on the hand commit. 12 legacy tests passed.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test` for the workspace. A test shows that a legacy-exempt record that later gains an entry is refused as append-only, and that the original record is unchanged.
criteria.evidence: `a_legacy_exempt_record_that_gains_an_entry_is_refused` asserts `RecordsError::Refused`, the same records tip, identical blob bytes and the original parsed record. `a_records_history_in_which_the_record_changed_is_a_finding` gives `LegacyExemptChanged` on the forced commit. The workspace `cargo test --locked` is Athena's recorded run (1142 tests passed).

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-gate`. A test with C0 as a parameter shows that commits after C0 are judged only by the records-only rule from part 1 (an unattributed post-C0 commit is a finding, and a pre-C0 commit is never judged by attribution). A second test shows that a commit exactly at C0 is judged by the legacy rule.
criteria.evidence: `commits_after_c0_are_judged_only_by_records_and_pre_c0_never_by_attribution` asserts base == C0, checked == 1, findings == [Unattributed] for the later commit, and no finding for the root or C0. `a_commit_exactly_at_c0_is_judged_by_the_legacy_rule` gives a LegacyHistory finding and no Unattributed finding when the entry is absent, and passes with checked == 0 when it is present. Both passed, along with the existing attribution tests.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`. A test builds the legacy-exempt record from the built-in or repository athena.toml's current [history] exempt list. The record has exactly seven entries, the six listed plus 02837e0, each with a non-empty reason taken from the athena.toml comments. It validates under LegacyExempt::validate, and nothing is written to any git ref.
criteria.evidence: `legacy_exempt_record_holds_the_seven_entries_with_reasons_and_writes_nothing` uses `builtin_config()`, which is `include_str!` of the repository athena.toml. It asserts len == 7, the order matches the seven names, every reason is non-empty, `validate` returns Ok, the change round-trips, and the records ref is absent (RecordsTip::Missing). I compared the REASONS table with athena.toml lines 136-155: the reasons match. 49c6ac1 uses the header comment (§7.3).

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`. Both are clean.
criteria.evidence: Clippy finished with no warnings, and fmt --check produced no output. Athena's recorded `-D warnings` clippy run and its fmt run also passed.

criteria.criterion: The existing history-check logic is reused, not copied: the exempt list is the only thing that differs, and check_history's existing tests pass unchanged.
criteria.evidence: In the history.rs diff, `check_history` now delegates to `check_history_with_exempt(git, tip, None)`, and the only logic change is `exempt: exempt.unwrap_or_else(|| tip_config.history.exempt.clone())`. No test bodies were edited, and legacy.rs has no copy of the walk. 13 history-filtered tests passed.

criteria.criterion: athena.toml, defaults.toml and the workflows are unchanged, and no function chooses a value for C0. The module docs say C0 is a caller-supplied parameter and cite design section 4 and decision D111.
criteria.evidence: The diff stat lists only CHANGELOG.md, the two history.rs files, attribution.rs, legacy.rs, lib.rs and the design doc. Every C0 is a function argument; there is no const or chooser. The legacy.rs module doc says "C0 is a caller-supplied parameter" and cites §4, §10 and D111.

criteria.criterion: The attribution.rs module doc comment, which says the legacy rule will come later, is updated to describe the rule as built.
criteria.evidence: The sentence "the legacy rule will later" was removed. A new section, "# The legacy rule", describes `check_attribution_with_legacy`, the inclusive caller-supplied C0, the exempt list from `legacy-exempt.json`, and the walk starting after C0.

findings.summary: A changed record is detected by matching the path as a substring of the audit message, so a file such as `x/legacy-exempt.json` would also match.
findings.evidence: `if problem.detail.contains(LEGACY_EXEMPT_PATH)` is applied to `audit_history`'s free-text detail ("changes {path}, which its first parent held"). `audit_history` should return the path as structured data instead.

findings.summary: The seven per-name tests build the same kind of commit (a README hand edit) for every name; only the reason text differs. They cannot show behaviour specific to each commit's real shape (a second root, a squash of several landings).
findings.evidence: `world()` is identical on every iteration of the NAMES loop. The accepted reading allows constructed repos, so this is not a criterion failure.

findings.summary: The design doc says `[history] exempt` stays "until job 8"; §4 says "until stage 2".
findings.evidence: §4 lines 123-125 and the new part 2 note use different milestones for the same thing. They are probably the same point, but the doc should use one term.

summary: The candidate adds the legacy rule as the request and design §4 describe. `check_history_with_exempt` changes only where `check_history` gets its exempt list; `check_history` now just calls it with `None`. The new `legacy.rs` module judges commits up to and including a caller-supplied C0 by that history check, reading the exempt list from `legacy-exempt.json` on the records tip. Commits after C0 go through the part 1 records-only walk, which now starts at C0. `legacy_exempt_record` builds the record from athena.toml's seven entries, using reasons copied from its comments (a personal name in one comment became "the user"), and writes nothing. Append-only is enforced by the existing `RecordsWriter` refusal, which a test covers. A forced rewrite in the records history is reported as a finding. I ran the targeted legacy, history and attribution tests, plus `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`; all passed in this snapshot. For the full test suite I cite Athena's recorded `cargo test --locked` run. athena.toml, defaults.toml and the workflows are untouched, and no code picks a C0. I found only minor issues.
